databaseName: Section 7 - Generative AI Model Fundamentals Vocabulary

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Transformer Architecture"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Transformer Architecture - Neural network architecture that LLMs are built on, using self-attention mechanisms instead of sequential RNN processing to enable parallel computation

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is a neural network architecture that LLMs are built on, using self-attention mechanisms instead of sequential RNN processing to enable parallel computation
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Transformer Architecture

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "self-attention"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: self-attention - FFNN concept. For RNN we have 'attention' awareness of previous tokens translated. This is a sequential process. "Self Attention" move that 'previous tokens' or hidden state into its own memory space 'self attention' making parallel processing possible

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is an FFNN concept. For RNN we have 'attention' awareness of previous tokens translated. This is a sequential process. _____ moves that 'previous tokens' or hidden state into its own memory space making parallel processing possible
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: self-attention

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Attention Weight"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Attention Weight - The weight or score that determines how much focus is allocated to each word/token when computing attention relationships between tokens

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the weight or score that determines how much focus is allocated to each word/token when computing attention relationships between tokens
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Attention Weight

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Scaled dot-product attention"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Scaled dot-product attention - A similarity function used in self-attention that computes attention scores by taking the dot product of query and key vectors, then scaling them

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is a similarity function used in self-attention that computes attention scores by taking the dot product of query and key vectors, then scaling them
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Scaled dot-product attention

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Scaled data product attention"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Scaled data product attention - Same as scaled dot-product attention; alternative naming for the dot product similarity function used to compute attention scores

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the same as scaled dot-product attention; it is alternative naming for the dot product similarity function used to compute attention scores
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Scaled data product attention

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are "q, k, v vectors"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: q, k, v vectors - Q (Query), K (Key), and V (Value) vectors used to calculate attention weights in transformers and feed-forward neural networks. Each token gets these three vectors by multiplying its embedding against learned weight matrices

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ are Q (Query), K (Key), and V (Value) vectors used to calculate attention weights in transformers and feed-forward neural networks. Each token gets these three vectors by multiplying its embedding against learned weight matrices
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: q, k, v vectors

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "interleaved sinusoidal function"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: interleaved sinusoidal function - Mathematical function used for positional encoding that captures the position of tokens relative to others and works on inputs of any length

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is a mathematical function used for positional encoding that captures the position of tokens relative to others and works on inputs of any length
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: interleaved sinusoidal function

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are "logits"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: logits - The output probabilities for each token being the right next token in the sequence, computed by multiplying the decoder output vector with token embeddings

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ are the output probabilities for each token being the right next token in the sequence, computed by multiplying the decoder output vector with token embeddings
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: logits

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are "tokens"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: tokens - numerical representation of words or parts of words (numeric)

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ are numerical representations of words or parts of words (numeric)
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: tokens

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What are "Embeddings"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Embeddings - Mathematical representations (vectors) that encode "meaning" of a token (hence, spanish, german, english may map to the same token because we are working with 'meaning')

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ are mathematical representations (vectors) that encode "meaning" of a token (hence, spanish, german, english may map to the same token because we are working with 'meaning')
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Embeddings

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Top P"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Top P - Threshold probability of a token inclusion (higher => greater randomness)

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the threshold probability of a token inclusion (higher => greater randomness)
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Top P

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Top K"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Top K - Alternative to top p instead of "top probability" where "top K" candidates exist for inclusion. Higher K, higher randomness

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is an alternative to top p instead of "top probability" where "top K" candidates exist for inclusion. Higher K, higher randomness
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Top K

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "temperature"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: temperature - the level of randomness in selecting the next word in the output from those tokens. Higher temperature -> more random. Low temperature -> more consistent (less random)

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the level of randomness in selecting the next word in the output from those tokens. Higher _____ -> more random. Low _____ -> more consistent (less random)
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: temperature

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Context window"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Context window - The number of tokens an LLM can process at once

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the number of tokens an LLM can process at once
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Context window

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Max tokens"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Max tokens - Limit for the total number of tokens (on input or output)

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the limit for the total number of tokens (on input or output)
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Max tokens

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: What is "Embedding Space"?
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Embedding Space - The high-dimensional vector space (often thousands of dimensions) where embeddings exist. The distance between vectors in this space determines how semantically close or related tokens are to each other

questionsWithAnswers.questionText: Fill in the blank: _____ is the high-dimensional vector space (often thousands of dimensions) where embeddings exist. The distance between vectors in this space determines how semantically close or related tokens are to each other
questionsWithAnswers.answerText: Embedding Space
